title: P4: Jev shadow-routing evaluation — scorecard.routing_eval joins the shadow rows to accepted-task outcomes (first-pass, fix rounds, tokens and cost to accepted, gate and review results) for agree vs disagree dispatches, grouped by complexity band, task class, executor and per-signal threshold, reports coverage, skip reasons, Jev latency and cost, and declares insufficient evidence below a configured sample size; CLI scorecard --routing; baseline snapshots include the summary
spec:
Phase I P4 (brief .orchestrator/phase-i-program.md, section P4: disagreement is not improvement; the hypothetical must predict better downstream outcomes; compare by complexity, task type, executor, classification). Base goal/T-0445 after P3 (T-0471) merges: shadow rows via bus.log_run role jev_route with fields task, goal_id, mode, eligible, baseline, hypothetical, agrees, signals, confidence, evidence, latency_ms, usage, cache, error; pipeline.jev_route on the task; P0 per-task metrics in scorecard.efficiency (first_pass, fix_rounds, tokens, cost, tokens_to_first_green, gate_reds) and P2a executor_economics.
1. scorecard.routing_eval(root=STATE, min_samples=None) -> dict: rows = jev_route rows read through _attributed; each joined to its task's lineage root outcome from the efficiency per-task table (accepted or not, first_pass, fix_rounds, gate_reds, tokens, cost, tokens_to_first_green, review request_changes count) plus the executor that actually ran. Groups: overall; agree (baseline == hypothetical) vs disagree; by band; by task_class; by baseline executor; and per signal key, split at p >= 0.6 vs below. For each group: n, accepted share, first_pass_rate (defined count), fix_round_rate, avg_fix_rounds, median tokens_to_accepted, median cost_to_accepted, gate_red share, review request_changes share. Also: coverage (dispatches with a classification / all execute dispatches in the window), skip_reasons histogram (mode off, single eligible, budget, disabled, cache hit, error), jev_latency_ms median and p95, jev_usage tokens and usd totals. Evidence verdict: "insufficient" when the disagree group has fewer than min_samples rows (default [jev.routing].min_eval_samples = 20), else "collected"; the dict never claims improvement, it reports the numbers side by side with the defined counts (H1 rule: None for undefined).
2. CLI: orchestrator scorecard --routing [--json]: text tables for agree vs disagree and per-signal splits with n and defined counts on every row, a coverage and cost footer, and the evidence verdict line; --json dumps the dict.
3. baseline.save includes routing_eval(root) under efficiency.routing so P5's decision compares snapshots; baseline.compare reports the agree vs disagree deltas and the verdict without flagging them as non-inferiority metrics.
Tests tests/test_scorecard.py (synthetic jev_route rows and tasks): test_routing_eval_joins_rows_to_outcomes_by_lineage_root, test_routing_eval_agree_vs_disagree_groups_and_defined_counts, test_routing_eval_per_signal_threshold_split, test_routing_eval_coverage_and_skip_reasons, test_routing_eval_insufficient_below_min_samples, test_routing_eval_none_when_no_rows; tests/test_cli.py::test_cli_scorecard_routing_text_and_json; tests/test_baseline.py::test_baseline_includes_routing_eval_and_compare_reports_it. Existing tests green; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0; commit with the task id including every named test; report sha and failures only.
acceptance: routing_eval reports agree vs disagree outcomes with defined counts, coverage, skip reasons, Jev latency and cost, and the evidence verdict; it never asserts improvement
